title: Can two different estimates of a sum both be right?
description: {{NAME_2}} and {{NAME_1}} estimate the sum of two numbers near eight lakh and nine lakh, one rounding down and one rounding up. The board checks both estimates, finds whose is closer, compares the sum with two given numbers, and adds exactly. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking the two estimates cannot both be right.
teaching_notes: One idea: rounding down gives an estimate below the real sum and rounding up gives one above it, so two different estimates can both be right. Ask the class what rounding down does to a number before the estimates are checked. Watch for students who think two different estimates cannot both be correct.

source: Check the estimates of 4,63,128 + 4,19,682 by Roxie (near 8,00,000, more) and Estu (near 9,00,000, less). Say whose is closer, whether the sum is above or below 8,50,000 and 8,83,128, and find the exact sum
video_script.why: The child can round to a place and compare numbers, and now uses rounding down and rounding up to trap a sum.
video_script.substitution: Rounding both numbers down gives an estimate below the sum, rounding both up gives one above it, and the exact sum shows whose estimate is closer.
video_script.anchor: The sum 4,63,128 + 4,19,682 with a number line from 8,00,000 to 9,00,000 under it.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that the two estimates are different and thinks they cannot both be right. One rounds down and the other rounds up, so the real sum lies between them and both are right.

final_answer.value: Both estimates are correct; {{NAME_1}}'s is closer; more than 8,50,000; less than 8,83,128; exact sum 8,82,810
final_answer.spoken: both estimates are correct, the estimate of {{NAME_1}} is closer, the sum is more than eight lakh fifty thousand and less than eight lakh eighty three thousand one hundred twenty eight, and the exact sum is eight lakh eighty two thousand eight hundred ten

names.{{NAME_1}}: Eshwarappa's son, who estimates the sum near nine lakh and less
names.{{NAME_2}}: Eshwarappa's daughter, who estimates the sum near eight lakh and more

never_show: the exact sum written whole before the answer beat
maths_rules: rounding both down to 4,00,000 gives 8,00,000, and both numbers are bigger, so the sum is more than 8,00,000
rounding both up a little to 4,70,000 and 4,30,000 gives 9,00,000, and both numbers are smaller, so the sum is less than 9,00,000
distance from 9,00,000 is 9,00,000 − 8,82,810 = 17,190; distance from 8,00,000 is 8,82,810 − 8,00,000 = 82,810; 17,190 is smaller, so the estimate near 9,00,000 is closer
4,63,128 is more than 4,50,000 and 4,19,682 is more than 4,00,000, so the sum is more than 8,50,000
video_script.design: One idea: round down to get below, round up to get above, and both can be right. Wrong idea: Keeko says different estimates cannot both be right. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, {{NAME_2}} rounds both numbers down to four lakh.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four lakh plus four lakh is eight lakh. Both numbers are bigger than four lakh, so the sum is more than eight lakh.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>{{NAME_1}} rounds both numbers up a little, to four lakh seventy thousand and four lakh thirty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Together they make nine lakh. Both numbers are smaller than these, so the sum is less than nine lakh.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: add in groups: 128 + 682 = 810; 63 + 19 = 82 thousand; 4 + 4 = 8 lakh. Distance below 9,00,000: 17,190. Distance above 8,00,000: 82,810. 17,190 is smaller

marks.m4: the distance 82,810 is shown on the number line above 8,00,000

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, add the numbers in groups. One hundred twenty eight plus six hundred eighty two is eight hundred ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Sixty three thousand plus nineteen thousand is eighty two thousand. Four lakh plus four lakh is eight lakh.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The sum is seventeen thousand one hundred ninety below nine lakh.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>It is eighty two thousand eight hundred ten above eight lakh.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The smaller distance is from nine lakh, so {{NAME_1}} is closer.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, compare with eight lakh fifty thousand. The first number is more than four lakh fifty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The second number is more than four lakh, so the sum is more than eight lakh fifty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Eight lakh eighty three thousand one hundred twenty eight is the first number plus four lakh twenty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The second number is less than four lakh twenty thousand, so the sum is less than that.
